diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the data are well-conditioned and the classes are separable, convergence is fast.

issues.failure_explanation: Strict convexity alone does not imply existence of a minimizer. For linearly separable data the logistic empirical risk is strictly convex but its infimum 0 is not attained: with one sample (x,y)=(1,1), R(theta)=log(1+e^{-theta}) has no minimizer (the iterates diverge in norm), so the unconditional claim of a unique minimizer is false. The same paragraph even presents the separable case as the favorable one. Uniqueness would additionally require the x_i to span the parameter space.

failure_location.quote: This function is smooth and (strictly) \emph{convex}, and therefore its minimization admits a unique minimizer.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard qualifier: a (unique) minimizer exists only when the data are not linearly separable (and, for uniqueness, the inputs span the parameter space); otherwise the infimum is approached only as ||theta||->infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The stated existence/uniqueness guarantee for the logistic-regression ERM, and the claim that separable data give fast convergence, are unreliable in precisely the regime the text highlights.
issues.title: Logistic ERM wrongly claimed to admit a unique minimizer, including for separable data
issues.why_classification: A local added qualifier fully restores the claim; the model, the convexity discussion, and all surrounding content survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: inverse Hessian~$H^{-1}$ of the inner objective.

issues.failure_explanation: For the inner problem min_theta sum_i gamma_i R_i(theta), the stationarity condition is grad_theta(sum_i gamma_i R_i)(theta*)=0. Differentiating with respect to gamma_j gives H * (d theta*/d gamma_j) + grad_theta R_j(theta*) = 0 with H the Hessian of the inner weighted objective, so dC/dgamma_j = -(grad_theta C)^T H^{-1} grad_theta R_j(theta*). As printed, the third factor is the Hessian grad^2_theta R_j (an n x n matrix), making the product a row vector rather than the claimed scalar component; additionally H is defined as grad_theta R_m(theta*,gamma), a gradient, while the text itself calls H^{-1} 'the inverse Hessian of the inner objective'. The printed formula is dimensionally inconsistent and is not the hypergradient of the stated bilevel problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace grad^2_theta R_j(theta*) by the gradient grad_theta R_j(theta*) and define H := grad^2_theta (sum_i gamma_i R_i)(theta*), i.e., the Hessian of the inner weighted objective.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed 'exact update' for the loss weights gamma, the only formula given for bilevel loss balancing, is invalid as written; only the qualitative statement that the response is governed by an inverse Hessian survives.
issues.title: Bilevel hypergradient formula differentiates the wrong derivative and misdefines H
issues.why_classification: A local two-symbol correction restores the standard implicit-differentiation formula; the bilevel-balancing discussion and all practical claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: In the displayed L_grad, the inner average (1/N) sum_{j=1}^N ||gamma_i grad R_i(theta)|| r_i^zeta does not depend on the summation index j: both the norm and the rate r_i carry the outer index i (and r_i is built only from loss ratios, with no j). The 'average' therefore equals its single summand and the objective degenerates to sum_i ||gamma_i grad R_i|| |1 - r_i^zeta|; minimizing it over gamma>0 drives every weight with r_i^zeta != 1 to zero, contradicting the stated goal of equalizing per-loss gradient magnitudes and the cited GradNorm method, whose target for component i is the average of the per-loss gradient norms scaled by r_i^zeta. The intended formula cannot be recovered without choosing which factors must carry the index j, i.e., a mathematical repair rather than a forced symbol change.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the j-dependence of the target, e.g., target_i = ((1/N) sum_j ||gamma_j grad_theta R_j(theta)||) r_i^zeta as in the cited method, and keep the described single gradient-descent step on each gamma_i.
issues.overall_effect: The only mathematical characterization of GradNorm in the paper is wrong: the displayed surrogate is degenerate and its minimization would shrink all weights rather than equalize gradient contributions, so the description of the adaptive-weighting procedure and of its cheap update is unsupported.
issues.title: GradNorm surrogate objective contains a degenerate inner average (index error)
issues.why_classification: A contained index repair of one displayed formula; the surrounding heuristic description of adaptive weighting survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: applied to a strongly convex quadratic model with constant Hessian $H = \nabla^2 f(\theta)$ and step size $0 < \alpha < 2/\lambda_{\max}(H)$.
It is well known that the GD iterates satisfy the following classical contraction bound (see, e.g.,~\cite[Section~3.2]{nocedal2006numerical}):
Thus, if $\lambda_{\min}(H)$ is very small, the contraction factor approaches one and progress becomes arbitrarily slow.

issues.failure_explanation: For GD on a strongly convex quadratic the per-step contraction factor is max_i |1 - alpha lambda_i|, which equals (kappa-1)/(kappa+1) only at the optimal step alpha* = 2/(lambda_min + lambda_max). The claim asserts the bound for every 0 < alpha < 2/lambda_max. Counterexample: H = diag(1,10) (kappa = 10, claimed factor 9/11 = 0.818) with alpha = 0.15 gives a worst-mode factor |1-0.15| = 0.85 > 9/11, violating the bound after one step; as alpha -> 0 the factor tends to 1 for any kappa. Only the optimal-step version is the classical result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the optimal step alpha = 2/(lambda_min(H)+lambda_max(H)), or replace the factor by max_i |1 - alpha lambda_i|, which is valid for every 0 < alpha < 2/lambda_max(H).
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative argument that a small lambda_min forces the contraction factor toward one, used to connect NTK/Hessian conditioning to slow GD progress, is based on an incorrectly stated hypothesis range; the qualitative conclusion survives only under the corrected optimal-step statement.
issues.title: Quadratic GD contraction bound asserted for every step size but holds only at the optimal step
issues.why_classification: A one-clause hypothesis repair (optimal step, or the max_i|1-alpha lambda_i| factor) preserves the intended conclusion about ill-conditioning; no result or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand side minimizes over k an expression that does not depend on k: it contains only the K-dependent average theta-bar_K, which is never defined in this theorem, so the claim is vacuous as printed (the standard quantity would be min_k E||grad f(theta_k)||^2). The step size and the bound involve the constant L_f, which is defined nowhere in the paper (only L_max = max_i L_i is introduced), and the bound uses Delta_f^star while only Delta_f is defined. Under the literal reading (gradient norm at the averaged iterate, without convexity, which this section explicitly does not assume) no supported proof route exists, since averaging iterates is justified only under convexity. No proof of the theorem is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem in the standard form: min_{k<=K-1} E||grad f(theta_k)||^2 <= 2(f(theta_0)-inf f)/(alpha K) + alpha L sigma^2 with alpha as given and L a defined smoothness constant, defining L_f and Delta_f^star (or removing them); the claimed O(K^{-1/2}) / O(epsilon^{-2}) guarantee then survives in its standard shape.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem th:nonconvex, the section's only nonconvex stationarity guarantee, does not state a well-defined mathematical claim, and the accompanying prose ('we need O(epsilon^-2) iterations to drive the norm of the gradient below the tolerance epsilon') inherits the defect.
issues.title: Nonconvex SGD theorem is ill-formed: vacuous minimization and undefined constants
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained restatement of a standard result (the cited handbook contains the correct form); the rate guarantee survives, but several coordinated statement defects must be repaired, so it exceeds a minor fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The refined NTK,  $\Theta_7 = \tfrac{1}{7}\sum_{j=1}^7 J(x_j)J(x_j)^\top$, exhibits $\lambda_{\max}\approx 4.0$ and $\lambda_{\min}\approx 0.30$,
in turn reducing the condition number to $\kappa(\Theta_7)\!\approx\!13$.

issues.failure_explanation: With phi_1'' = -2 and phi_2'' = 2 - 12x + 12x^2, the Jacobians J(x) = (2, 12x - 12x^2 - 2) are independent of f and theta, and at the five uniform points they are (2,-0.92), (2,0.52), (2,1), (2,0.52), (2,-0.92) - separated by roughly 50 degrees, so the premise that they are 'nearly collinear' is false. The resulting Theta_5 = [[4, 0.08], [0.08, 0.64672]] has eigenvalues ~4.002 and ~0.645 (trace 4.647, det 2.580), hence kappa ~ 6.2, not ~200; in particular lambda_min ~ 0.02 is impossible since lambda_min <= (Theta_5)_{22} = 0.647. For the refined set the same computation gives eigenvalues ~4.071 and ~0.714, i.e., kappa ~ 5.7, not ~13. The advertised dramatic improvement (kappa 200 -> 13, lambda_min 0.02 -> 0.30) is therefore not produced by the model as defined.

failure_location.quote: has eigenvalues $\lambda_{\max}\approx 4.1$ and $\lambda_{\min}\approx 0.02$, yielding a condition number $\kappa(\Theta_5)\!\approx\!200$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the spectra of Theta_5 and Theta_7 for the stated surrogate (giving kappa ~ 6.2 and ~5.7) and weaken the accompanying claims accordingly, or replace the surrogate/point sets so that the quoted numbers hold.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only quantitative demonstration that adaptive collocation sampling sharply improves NTK conditioning (kappa ~ 200 -> ~13, lambda_min 0.02 -> 0.30) is numerically false; the illustrative example and the 'increases sharply' narrative lose their support, while the separate qualitative Weyl-monotonicity argument in the same section is unaffected.
issues.title: 1D Poisson example's NTK eigenvalues and condition numbers contradict the defined model
issues.why_classification: Repairing requires recomputation and withdrawal of the advertised quantitative effect (kappa 200 -> 13), so it is more than minor; but the section's qualitative message and the supporting Weyl argument remain intact, so no major loss or new proof architecture is involved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the sample-wise objective function becomes $f_i(\theta) = \ell\bigl(h_\theta(M^{-1}x),\, y\bigr)$,

issues.failure_explanation: For f_i(theta) = ell(h_theta(M^{-1}x), y), the chain rule with respect to theta gives grad_theta f_i = (d h_theta(w)/d theta)^T grad_z ell evaluated at w = M^{-1}x; the factor M^{-1} belongs to differentiation with respect to the input x, not theta. The displayed identity is false as a formula for the parameter gradient: e.g., with h_theta(z) = theta^T z and ell(a,y) = (1/2)(a-y)^2, the true gradient is M^{-1}x (x^T M^{-T} theta - y), while the printed formula yields an extra factor M^{-1}. Equivalently, the printed expression is the gradient with respect to the input x, mislabeled as the theta-gradient. Since two different repairs (delete M^{-1}, or relabel the gradient as one with respect to x) lead to different meanings, this is not a single forced correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the chain rule: grad_theta f_i = (d h_theta(w)/d theta)^T grad_z ell with w = M^{-1}x (no M^{-1} factor), or restate the displayed formula as the gradient with respect to the input x with the corresponding transpose.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed identity that supports the claim that input transformations 'alter both the search direction and its magnitude' is false as written; the qualitative claim about data-space preconditioning is unaffected, but the supporting computation is wrong.
issues.title: Data-space preconditioning gradient formula is wrong (spurious M^{-1} factor)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one displayed identity; the qualitative data-space preconditioning discussion and all downstream prose survive.
